item.title: PN demands studies behind Budget 2027 measures on foreign workers and tourists
item.description: The Nationalist Party has asked the government to publish the studies behind its Budget 2027 measures targeting non-EU workers and tourists, and to explain how the extra revenue will be spent. PN deputy leader Alex Perici Calascione said the higher charges alone cannot address the strain on tourism and infrastructure, while PN leader Alex Borg said businesses should not be made to pay for the government's mistakes. Prime Minister Robert Abela said employers should help cover the cost of services used by third-country nationals, and GWU general secretary Kevin Camilleri branded the package "purely populist".
item.content:encoded:
The Nationalist Party has asked the government to publish the studies behind its Budget 2027 measures targeting non-EU workers and tourists, and to explain how the extra revenue will be spent. PN deputy leader Alex Perici Calascione said the higher charges alone cannot address the strain on tourism and infrastructure, while PN leader Alex Borg said businesses should not be made to pay for the government's mistakes. Prime Minister Robert Abela said employers should help cover the cost of services used by third-country nationals, and GWU general secretary Kevin Camilleri branded the package "purely populist".

Sources: Times of Malta, Malta Today, Lovin Malta, Malta Independent

item.title: Mater Dei emergency capacity to double as health minister unveils Budget 2027 care package
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg and Parliamentary Secretary Deo Debattista presented the health and active-ageing measures of Budget 2027, including a €120 million expansion of Mater Dei that will lift emergency department treatment spaces from 35 to 70 and add paediatric emergency capacity. Borg said a regeneration plan for Gozo General Hospital must be drawn up by year end, alongside nine new outpatient clinics and completion of the Gozo helipad. He did not give figures for the nurses, doctors and other professionals needed to staff the expanded facilities, pointing instead to contracts with private operators.

item.title: BOV raises 2026 profit guidance after €189.6m nine-month result
item.description: Bank of Valletta reported profit before tax of €189.6 million for the first nine months of 2026, broadly in line with €192.1 million a year earlier, and raised the lower end of its full-year guidance to €230 million. Operating income rose 6% to €387.1 million on a 10.6% increase in net interest income, gross loans grew 9.9% to €8.9 billion and customer deposits reached €14.6 billion. Chairperson Gordon Cordina attributed the year-on-year dip to the non-recurrence of 2025 income items and continued strategic investment.

item.title: APS Bank posts record €34.5m pre-tax profit in first nine months
item.description: APS Bank reported record pre-tax group profits of €34.5 million for January to September, almost double the same period a year earlier, with post-tax profits more than doubling to about €23 million. Net interest income grew by more than a third to €77.7 million, the net interest margin strengthened to 2.23% from 1.8%, and interest costs dropped a quarter to €25.6 million. The bank attributed the improvement to growth in retail and commercial lending, a stronger treasury contribution and lower funding costs.

item.title: Deposit scheme buyers now wait over 16 months to complete purchases
item.description: Applicants approved under the Housing Authority's 10% Deposit Scheme took an average 481 days between approval and executing the final property contract in 2026, up from 348 days in 2022. Figures given by Housing Minister Owen Bonnici in reply to a parliamentary question by PN MP Stanley Zammit show approval times improved from 18 to 14 days while the search-and-contract stage lengthened. End to end, the average wait from completed application to final contract reached 495 days this year against 366 days in 2022.

item.title: Turkish firm GiMAS opens €10m green energy plant at Ħal Far
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela inaugurated a €10 million investment by GiMAS Malta Heavy Industries at Ħal Far, marking a new industrial sector in Malta producing advanced components for sustainable energy. The 8,400 square metre facility will initially employ just over 40 people, rising to 60 by its fifth year, and is the Turkish group's first plant of its kind in the European Union. Abela said the project demonstrated Malta's economic stability and its ability to attract investment despite international challenges.

item.title: Work starts on 89-home social housing project in Kirkop
item.description: Excavation has begun on a new social housing development in Kirkop comprising 89 apartments across eight residential blocks, with around 70 garage and parking spaces. Housing Minister Owen Bonnici put the cost at roughly €8.2 million, excluding lifts, and said the scheme forms part of the government's efforts to expand housing for vulnerable families. The minister described decent housing as essential for families and individuals to enjoy greater stability.

item.title: 56 people found sleeping rough given shelter over four months
item.description: A total of 56 people found sleeping on Malta's streets were taken off the streets and accommodated at reception centres run by the Agency for the Welfare of Asylum Seekers over the past four months, Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said. The announcement follows controversy over people sleeping in the underpass beneath St Anne Street in Floriana, where police intervened to clear the passageway. Bedingfield said the government's approach is based on "security and dignity" and confirmed a man removed from the Floriana subway had been offered shelter.

item.title: Fleur-de-Lys Road to close partially from Saturday for resurfacing
item.description: Resurfacing works on the lower part of Fleur-de-Lys Road in Birkirkara start on Saturday, timed to coincide with the school mid-term holidays, Infrastructure Malta said. Northbound traffic from Santa Venera towards Birkirkara will flow as normal, while southbound traffic will be diverted through Psaila Street. The works cover the lower, busier section of the road.

item.title: Heavy congestion hits several roads from 4pm
item.description: Severe congestion affected several main roads around Malta from around 4pm, with some journeys taking more than an hour. Traffic maps showed slow-moving and congested sections around Msida, Gżira, Marsa and the harbour approaches, with roads in some areas barely moving. One commuter reported being stuck for over an hour while travelling from Valletta towards San Ġwann.

item.title: Air Serbia launches direct Malta–Niš flights twice weekly
item.description: Air Serbia has started operating direct flights between Malta and the Serbian city of Niš, with the inaugural service flown on 25 October. The route runs twice a week, on Wednesdays and Sundays, as part of the airline's winter schedule. Malta International Airport said the connection gives Serbian nationals working in Malta another way to travel between the two countries, and opens a new destination for Maltese visitors.

item.title: MP calls for action on exploitation risks at unlicensed massage parlours
item.description: MP Graziella Attard Previ told parliament that trafficking victims are often slow to come forward or give formal statements, and asked for concrete support and protection for them. She said the presence of some massage parlours in Malta raises exploitation risks, noting that no specific licence has been required for such establishments since 2016 while trafficking of adults carries six to 12 years' imprisonment. She stressed that any allegation of abuse or exploitation must be investigated by the authorities.

item.title: Pharmacies asked not to sell white powder and dust to certain youths
item.description: Pharmacies in San Pawl il-Baħar are being asked to be more vigilant about selling products such as white powder and dust in the run-up to Halloween. The local council and community police said in a joint notice dated 27 October that such products have been misused in past years, causing damage to residents' homes and property. Traders were asked to avoid selling the items to people who do not normally buy them, with particular attention to young people.

item.title: Man stole restaurant sunshades to buy medication for wife, court told
item.description: A 62-year-old man from Ħaż-Żabbar admitted stealing five sunshades worth about €500 each from two restaurants in Marsaxlokk over three consecutive days this month. He said he did it to buy medication for his wife, whose health problems had left the family under financial strain, and he returned one of the umbrellas. The magistrate deferred sentence and barred him from returning to Marsaxlokk in the meantime, and the court heard he is a recidivist who committed the offences while serving a suspended sentence.

item.title: Paola mayor's bank account frozen after council appealed planning permit
item.description: Paola mayor Jason Silvio said a developer froze his personal bank account after the local council appealed a Planning Authority permit for a multi-storey development in the town's Urban Conservation Area. Councillors suspended the council meeting in solidarity, and other mayors and ministers have expressed support for him. Prime Minister Robert Abela said the government will give the mayor the full protection of the State in the sequestration proceedings and in a damages case filed against him. The dispute concerns a proposed complex on Triq Ninu Cremona that the council says would affect the setting of a scheduled church.

item.title: Defence opens closing arguments in Lassana Cisse murder trial
item.description: Defence lawyer Edward Gatt told the jury in the trial of Lorin Scicluna, accused of killing Lassana Cisse, to disregard allegations and criticism directed at jurors who served in the separate Yorgen Fenech case. Gatt began closing arguments on Thursday morning, saying Scicluna must be presumed innocent and urging jurors to set aside any prejudice arising from the timing of the proceedings. Scicluna, a former Armed Forces of Malta soldier, broke down in tears on Wednesday, denying responsibility and blaming co-accused Francesco Fenech for the shooting that killed the Ivorian migrant in April 2019.

item.title: Three Gozo ministry officials acquitted over worker's death in Dwejra roof collapse
item.description: Joseph Cutajar, Vicky Xuereb and Joseph Xuereb were cleared of involuntary homicide and health-and-safety breaches over the death of maintenance worker Carmel Attard, 52. The court found the demolition work that led to Attard's death had never been authorised and that several required safety measures had not been implemented, but ruled the prosecution had failed to establish the accused's individual criminal responsibility. Attard was killed on 18 March 2021 when the concrete roof of a public toilet in Dwejra collapsed during renovation works.

item.title: Central Bank says Malta's economic indicators show a mixed bag
item.description: The Central Bank's latest economic update says Malta's growth has slowed, with some sectors performing strongly while others weaken. Tourist expenditure rose 14.9% in August on higher spending per night and per visitor, even as stays shortened, and consumer sentiment remained strong. The bank reports business conditions below their long-term average, a property market cooling from a period of exceptionally strong dynamics, and residential permits falling markedly back to their five-year average.

item.title: Non-EU nurses and carers spared one Budget fee but made to pay another
item.description: Health Minister Ian Borg said non-EU healthcare workers will not face the increased work permit fees introduced in Budget 2027, and that a 2025 legal notice slashing permit application and renewal fees for healthcare workers will remain in force. Those same workers will still be liable for the new annual €400 infrastructure contribution announced in the budget speech, as it applies to all non-EU nationals.

item.title: TCN long-term residency blocked by backlog in integration programme
item.description: Some third-country nationals have waited more than two years to enrol in or complete the I Belong integration programme, a key requirement for long-term resident status, raising fears they will be hit by the new Budget 2027 fees and charges. The programme is administered by the Human Rights Directorate and delivered with MCAST and the University of Malta. The prime minister said 5,205 applicants were on the waiting list as of January for a period not exceeding nine months.

item.title: GWU boss calls Budget measures against foreign workers 'purely populist'
item.description: General Workers' Union general secretary Kevin Camilleri said the punitive Budget 2027 measures targeting third-country nationals are 'purely populist', adding that 'as a socialist and leftist union, I can never agree with the measures'. He praised social measures protecting Maltese workers and pensioners but said the budget fails to address traffic and affordable housing.

item.title: Planning Authority seals off Mtaħleb residence in direct enforcement action
item.description: The Planning Authority sealed off a residence on Triq tal-Merħla in Mtaħleb following direct enforcement action over development carried out without planning permission. The owner is meanwhile facing daily fines, and the enforcement case has been running since 2023. The authority said the breaches concern land scheduled under Government Notice 400 of 1996.

item.title: PM Abela inaugurates €6m Buddha-Bar Malta investment
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela inaugurated Buddha-Bar Malta, a private investment exceeding €6 million that brings the international gastronomy and hospitality brand to the island, seating around 250 guests. Abela said the project reflects the government's shift toward higher quality, productivity and added value in tourism, and linked it to Budget 2027. The brand, founded in Paris in 1996, is marking its 30th anniversary this year.

item.title: Farmer feared for life after swarm of hornets attacked him in field
item.description: Farmer Anthony Bartolo says he feared for his life when a swarm of hornets chased and repeatedly stung him in his Burmarrad field, describing the insects as looking 'like a cloud'. He stopped the tractor cultivator he was driving and hurried away, but the hornets continued to sting him. When he called the Civil Protection Department for help he was told such incidents were outside its remit.

item.title: Catering association calls Budget 2027 'bittersweet'
item.description: The Association of Catering Establishments described Budget 2027 as 'bittersweet', welcoming corporation tax cuts for small businesses and new VAT guidelines while expressing serious concern about measures affecting non-EU workers. It called the €1,000 annual 'superbonus' for workers due by April 'certainly music to every worker's ears'.

item.title: Governance expert urges week-long TCN strike over Budget measures
item.description: Governance consultant David Spiteri Gingell said foreign workers should hold a week-long strike to highlight Malta's reliance on them, following the Budget measures targeting third-country nationals. In a LinkedIn post, he argued the country's dependence on TCN labour would be exposed by their absence for a week, and called on the TCN Alliance and trade unions to act.

item.title: AI could be used to spot grooming from players' in-game behaviour
item.description: University of Malta researcher Georgios Yannakakis said artificial intelligence could help detect child grooming in online games by analysing how players engage, and that studios should invest equally in AI that protects users from malicious agents. He warned that generative AI can create convincing avatars that talk to children, and cited a 2021 study with Ubisoft researchers that identified sanctioned players from gameplay data with at least 82% accuracy.
